paper_title: Astrophysical limits on very light axion-like particles from Chandra grating spectroscopy of NGC 1275
coupling_convention: canonical g_agamma in GeV^-1, as plotted
notes: Astrophysical limit on ALP-photon coupling from X-ray transparency of the Perseus cluster (Chandra HETG spectrum of NGC 1275). Mass-independent flat bound for m_a < 1e-12 eV. Quoted 99.7% credible-region upper limits: g_agamma < 6.3e-13 GeV^-1 (Model-A) and < 7.9e-13 GeV^-1 (Model-B); I emit the conservative Model-B value. The paper's CL is actually 99.7% (schema only allows 0.90/0.95; set to 0.95). Not a DM-density-dependent haloscope, so no local density assumed. Mass range spanned covers the model library (log10(m_a/eV) roughly -13.6 to -12) over which the limit is valid. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 30)) | Vision: AxionPhoton constraint from Chandra/HETG grating spectroscopy of NGC 1275 (Perseus cluster). Traced the heavy black 'HETG (99.7% excl.)' boundary of Model-A (top panel of Fig. 6), which is the tightest limit with a flat floor at g_agamma ~ 6.3e-13 GeV^-1 for m_a < 1e-12 eV, confirmed by text (g < 6.3e-13 model-A, 7.9e-13 model-B at 99.7%). Excluded region is above the line (light blue shading). The boundary steps up slightly near ~4e-17 eV, has small V-notch dips near 1e-13-3e-13 eV, and rises steeply above ~1e-12 eV. Note: boundary is a 99.7% credible region (not 90/95%); reported confidence_level field set to nearest allowed value 0.95. Also shown for reference: SN1987A (~5e-12), M87 (~2.6e-12), IAXO projection (dashed ~4.5e-12), FERMI. Y-axis multiplier confirmed as plain 10^-13..10^-11. | Calibration: No calibration needed (spot-check verify/stage2 raw_ratio=1.01 snapped to identity)
